text:
Standing tall with crimson feathers and a sinister beaked head, the herragath makes for a terrifying sight on the otherwise placid lake. 
To those that swim below the water, its red, sky-countering hue is all but unseen. Standing stock-still in the shallows, it waits for the sun 
to rise to its zenith when the frogs and fi sh of the Fenlands seek shelter beneath the dark canopy of the lily pads. Dozens of specialized 
leaf shaped scales spread outwards along its legs, and as prey nestle in close, the herragath will spear its beak downwards, impaling and 
securing another meal. As such a patient hunter requires absolute stillness, the bird has learned to mimic the surrounding predators, 
periodically emulating the roars, grunts and calls of fi erce beasts to keep the true hunters at a safe distance.
